biography_summary: Tran Dinh Long (born February 22, 1961, Thanh Mien District, Hai Duong Province) is a Vietnamese billionaire businessman and the founder and chairman of Hoa Phat Group Joint Stock Company (HPG), Vietnam's largest steel producer. Born into a rural family in northern Vietnam during the pre-Doi Moi period, Long graduated from the National Economics University in Hanoi in 1986 with a bachelor's degree in economics. In 1992, amid Vietnam's economic liberalization, he co-founded Hoa Phat as a small trading firm for second-hand construction equipment and parts in Hanoi, with close associate Tran Tuan Duong. In 1996, he pivoted the company toward steel pipe production. By 2007, Hoa Phat had evolved into a vertically integrated steel manufacturing conglomerate, launching the Hoa Phat Hai Duong Steel Complex with blast furnace technology. Under Long's leadership, the group expanded aggressively: the Dung Quat Steel Complex in Quang Ngai Province with over $7 billion in committed investments, diversification into agriculture (Hoa Phat Agricultural Development), real estate, and home appliances. Hoa Phat became Vietnam's largest steel producer, holding approximately 38% of the construction steel market, and ranked among the world's top 50 steel companies. Long first entered the Forbes billionaires list in 2018 with $1 billion; his net worth peaked at $3.3 billion in 2022. As of March 2026, his net worth was approximately $2.8 billion. Long is married to Vu Thi Hien, who holds approximately 7.44% of HPG shares. The couple has two children: Tran Vu Minh (being groomed as successor, received 42.8 million shares in 2023) and Tran Huyen Linh. Known for his 'xe lu' (steamroller) management philosophy emphasizing relentless vertical integration and steady market penetration, Long is commonly referred to as Vietnam's 'King of Steel.'
